test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A woman travelled at a speed of 20 m/min for 80 min, and at a speed of 65 m/min for 64 min. Her average speed (in m/min) is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **time** = 80 : 64 = 5 : 4

**Weighted Average Speed** = [(Speed₁ × Time Ratio₁) + (Speed₂ × Time Ratio₂)] ÷ Total Ratio

Average Speed = [(20 × 5) + (65 × 4)] ÷ (5 + 4)

Average Speed = [100 + 260] ÷ 9 = 360 ÷ 9 = 40 m/min

**∴ The correct answer is 40 m/min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ = 20 m/min, Time₁ = 80 min

Speed₂ = 65 m/min, Time₂ = 64 min

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac14c49a268f314f1ded47c51728c87a1c8b38aa73ca96197dc11e6a8cad740f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance₁ = 20 × 80 = 1600 m

⇒ Distance₂ = 65 × 64 = 4160 m

⇒ Total Distance = 1600 + 4160 = 5760 m

⇒ Total Time = 80 + 64 = 144 min

⇒ Average Speed = 5760 ÷ 144

⇒ Average Speed = 40 m/min

**∴ The correct answer is 40 m/min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |u − v|. In opposite directions, it is (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.</p
